header: The "Deep search (EDS)" tab of the user guide: one data file, read by src/components/help/EdsTab.tsx. EDS is the main strength of the app, so I gave it a tab of its own, and NOTHING about it is described on the other three tabs. The tab says (1) what EDS covers today, (2) what EDS is, with examples, (3) what the back end does when a circular is uploaded, page by page, and which AI model works at each step, (4) what happens, and which model works, when an executive asks a deep question, and (5) the questions to test it with, and how to make more. Nothing here is guessed. Every step and every model name below was read from the code (the upload route, geminiOcr.ts, chunking.ts, geminiEmbedding.ts, executiveSynthesis.ts, edsVerify.ts, edsStore.ts, synthesisIntent.ts) and is pinned by src/lib/help/edsGuide.selftest.ts, which reads those files and fails when the guide and the code disagree. The list of questions is the project's own test questions of 9 to 12 November 2026 (the panel, the gold set, the fresh set, and the corrected forms of three of them), de-duplicated; the selftest runs every one through the real detector (synthesisIntent.ts) so that "reaches EDS as typed" is a measured fact, not a claim. Keep this file free of server-only imports: it is drawn in the browser.

behaviours: the two OCR readers are the code's defaults: the main reader gemini-3.1-pro-preview, the checker gemini-3.8-flash
the router is the first chat model of the code (gemini-3.8-flash)
the writer uses the synthesis chain of the code (gemini-3.8-flash, then gemini-pro-latest, then gemini-3.8-flash) and the checker is the switch's model (gemini-3.8-flash)
the embedding model is gemini-embedding-001 with 768 numbers, a document type for what is stored and a query type for a question
the writer and the second reading both call the synthesis chain, with the thinking at low, and the briefing is stored only when it is good and the main model wrote it
the router is used only for the plain search (not for a line already sent as a deep question), with ONE chat model
an executive is a six-digit ticket starting with 4, checked in the staff directory by the server
an upload: only the HOD of C&IT or a delegate, PDF/PNG/JPG up to 15 MB, a headline and a date not in the future and not before 2000
the pages: drawn at 300 dpi as PNG and saved in Vercel Blob
the OCR: two Gemini readers at the same moment on a page shrunk to a 2,400-pixel JPEG; a page neither can read refuses the upload
the chunks are about 200 words and keep their page; the vectors are one per chunk and one for the whole circular's first 8,192 characters
the save: one transaction, the circular row and every chunk row (text, page number, vector), an audit row, a serial number within the year; a failure deletes the page pictures
the two special cases: a holiday-list circular is not read or chunked (a headline vector only); a roster is saved as rows
the search finds text by cosine similarity on the 768-number vectors in pgvector (<=>) and by the literal words

up to five circulars are given to the writer; one draft is written by default (a second only when the first is late: PERF.edsDrafts hedged); the question's identity is its words without capitals or punctuation and the archive's fingerprint
eight steps for an upload and eight for a question, numbered in order, each with a title and an explanation
a table of models for each: the upload (reader, checker, embeddings, no AI) and the question (no AI, router, vector, pgvector, writer, second reading, guards)
the scope says what EDS covers now, what it will cover later, that it is still being improved, and who may use it
what EDS is: a lead, four points and five examples, each example with the kind, a real question and what you get
every example question is one of the test questions of the list, word for word (so each can be tried)
the guide names no person, no ticket number, no phone and no e-mail address
it says before anything else to look at the uploaded circulars first, and to prepare a question only on those
the project's test files hold the panel (21), the gold set (9) and the fresh set (5)
23 questions, ids E01 to E23 in order, none written twice
EVERY question of the list reaches EDS as typed: the real detector scores 5 or more
a question that has an id in the project's test files is word for word that file's question (no typo, no drift)
every P, G or F id named in the list exists in the project's test files
EVERY question of the panel, the gold set and the fresh set is in the guide, either in the list or among those that do not reach EDS as typed (none is lost)
every question has a 'needs' line saying which circulars to look for in the list, and a kind
only the boundary question (E23) says that no circular covers it, and it carries a note saying what a good answer is
the three corrected questions say what they correct: E09 (the panel's P05, scored 4), E14 (P18, scored 3), E22 (P09, scored 1)
ten questions, each word for word the panel's, none reaching EDS as typed (below 5, or kept out by the people-data guard)
a question listed with another id (P07 = G04) is the same text in both of the project's files
where the reason says 'scores N', N is the detector's score
the people-data questions (P12, B02) are said to be kept out by the guard, and the detector agrees
the guide says a visitor who has not signed in is asked 'Are you an executive?' (Yes: sign in, then it runs by itself; No: the simple answer), and the code has that question
